metaData.originalTitle: Anthropic: 当 AI 开始构建自己
metaData.title: Anthropic: When AI Starts Building Itself
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: Anthropic publishes a long-form article, using external benchmarks and internal data to argue that AI systems are increasingly participating in their own R&D processes, and explores the trends, impacts, and three future scenarios of recursive self-improvement.
metaData.summary: This article is an in-depth piece published by the Anthropic Institute, originally titled "When AI builds itself." It systematically argues that AI systems are accelerating their involvement in the AI R&D pipeline, from writing code and running experiments to conducting evaluations, pointing towards the potential for recursive self-improvement in the future. The article is structured into several parts: first, it demonstrates the rapid capability improvement of models on external benchmarks (SWE-bench, CORE-Bench, METR long-horizon tasks); then, it reveals internal Anthropic data, including Claude writing over 80% of production code, an 8x increase in engineer per-capita output, and Claude's success rate on open-ended research tasks rising from 26% to 76%; it then discusses the shift in the human role from executor to direction-setter; finally, it proposes three future scenarios: trend stagnation, compound efficiency gains, and full recursive self-improvement, and explores the possibility of coordinated slowdown. The article is rich in data, rigorous in argumentation, and its analysis of future impacts is measured and boundary-aware.

mainPoints.point: AI systems are accelerating their involvement in all stages of AI R&D, from code writing to experiment execution.
mainPoints.explanation: Internal Anthropic data shows that Claude writes over 80% of production code, leading to an 8x increase in engineer per-capita output. On clearly defined experimental optimization tasks, Claude has already surpassed human-level performance.

mainPoints.point: AI is rapidly advancing in open-ended research and research judgment.
mainPoints.explanation: Claude's success rate on open-ended research tasks has increased from 26% to 76%. In tests for 'choosing the better next step,' the latest model outperforms human choices 64% of the time, suggesting that research taste may not be uniquely human.

mainPoints.point: Recursive self-improvement is not inevitable, but may arrive sooner than expected, bringing immense opportunities and risks.
mainPoints.explanation: The article proposes three future scenarios: trend stagnation, compound efficiency gains, and full recursive self-improvement. In the latter two scenarios, AI development becomes largely automated, the human role narrows, and alignment issues and risks of loss of control become core challenges.

mainPoints.point: Coordinated slowdown or pause is an ideal option, but implementation faces significant challenges.
mainPoints.explanation: A credible pause requires multi-party agreement, verifiable shutdown mechanisms, and conditions for triggering and lifting. Because training runs are easy to hide and incentives for defection are high, establishing a verification regime akin to arms control is urgent.

keyQuotes: The average amount of code shipped per quarter by an Anthropic engineer is 8 times higher than it was between 2021 and 2025.

If this trend continues, tasks that currently take skilled people days to complete this year could fall within the capability range of AI systems. By 2027, AI systems may be capable of tasks requiring weeks of human effort.
Edison said genius is 1% inspiration and 99% perspiration. But we are seeing that perspiration is increasingly being automated.
A meaningful slowdown or pause would require multiple well-resourced labs, at or near the frontier, across multiple countries, to agree to stop under the same conditions.

relatedArticles.title: Reverse Engineering and Systematic Analysis of Claude Code! Harness Engineering: A Complete Guide Based on Claude Code
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: By reverse-engineering over 500,000 lines of source code from Anthropic's official AI coding assistant, Claude Code, this article systematically proposes "Harness Engineering," an infrastructure design framework for AI Agents.

relatedArticles.title: Harness Engineering: How I Spent a Week Boosting AI Coding Rate to 90% in an Enterprise App
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article systematically introduces Harness Engineering, a new AI coding paradigm that elevates the AI code rate of an enterprise Java application from 25% to over 90% by building a four-element system of rules, skills, knowledge, and change management.

relatedArticles.title: Can Skill Documents Be Trained? SkillOpt: Turning Agent Experience into an Optimizable Manual
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article interprets Microsoft's paper SkillOpt, which proposes treating an Agent's Skill documents as trainable external states, enabling automated iterative optimization through mechanisms like rollout, reflection, bounded edits, and validation gates.

relatedArticles.title: OpenAI Weng Jiayi: A New Reinforcement Learning Paradigm of "Heuristic Learning"
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This paper proposes a new paradigm of "Heuristic Learning," where a coding agent continuously iterates hand-crafted rules and program strategies, achieving or surpassing the performance of Deep RL on multiple reinforcement learning benchmark tasks without training neural networks.

relatedArticles.title: How the Agentic Capabilities of Foundation Models Are Trained
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article systematically outlines how modern LLMs like GLM-5 build core reasoning, coding, and agentic capabilities through multi-stage training (pre-training, mid-training, SFT, and multi-stage RL) and complex data synthesis techniques.

relatedArticles.title: Understanding Hermes in One Article: How the New Top-Tier Agent Self-Evolves from Experience
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of the core innovation of the Hermes Agent—the Skills closed-loop system—detailing its complete implementation mechanism, from experience extraction and knowledge storage to intelligent retrieval and self-improvement, along with its engineering trade-offs and security considerations.

relatedArticles.title: Investing 10,000 RMB in AI: A Year of Tools, Practices, and Reflections
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: A systematic summary of a veteran developer's practical experience in the AI wave, covering everything from MAC toolchain optimization and Harness Engineering architectural constraints to building an Agent-driven automated learning loop.

relatedArticles.title: Harness Engineering — Agent Underperforming? It Might Not Be the Model's Fault
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article explores how the key to improving AI Agent performance lies in "Harness Engineering," which solves reliability issues by optimizing the execution environment, toolsets, and context management outside the model itself.

relatedArticles.title: What You Don't Know About Claude Code: Architecture, Governance, and Engineering Practices - Tw93
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of Claude Code's six-layer architecture and engineering practices, proposing a systematic Agent development methodology from context governance and skill design to a verification loop.

relatedArticles.title: Harness Is Not the Goal, Knowledge Is the Moat — Knowledge Accumulation Practices of an AI Engineering Delivery Team
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Based on the engineering delivery practices of an AI Team, this article proposes that knowledge accumulation is more important than workflow orchestration, and systematically introduces a complete methodology encompassing a five-layer knowledge storage architecture, a three-level maturity system, and how workflows serve knowledge accumulation.
